{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVAV-ec8AAAABZsUt5w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BmJKvzhDSpsA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BmJKv", "number": 30, "title": "Add simple per-project deletion from the project list", "body": "## Problem

gen3d currently lets users create and open projects but provides **no way to delete one in the Web UI or project HTTP API**. Users must stop the app and manually find a project UUID directory in `~/.gen3d`. This is both cumbersome and risky.

The UI should communicate the action through its layout and familiar controls—not long descriptions, secondary labels or a settings wizard. Project deletion is a basic project-list operation, separate from resetting the entire gen3d store.

## Expected outcome

Add **Delete project** directly to the **Home / Projects** list and/or project sidebar:

- A compact, discoverable per-project **⋯** action menu (or similarly conventional affordance) with **Delete**. Put the action where a user expects to manage that project; do not add permanent explanatory panels, multiple confirmation steps or a separate administration screen.
- Clicking Delete opens **one concise confirmation dialog** showing the **actual project name**, an explicit short warning that the project and its generated data will be permanently deleted, and **Cancel / Delete** actions. Cancel, Escape or dismissal must not delete anything; destructive confirmation is not preselected.
- After successful deletion, remove that project's entry immediately from navigation and the home grid. If the deleted project was selected, clear its persisted browser selection and return to Home / Projects (or another valid project), with a sensible empty state if none remain. Other open tabs should refresh from the shared server and drop the deleted selection.
- Implement a **real project-specific server/storage deletion**, not merely hiding a card. Remove the selected project's managed directory, `project.json`, image/model artifacts, run/node checkpoints, history and generated versions so it remains deleted after a server restart. Do **not** remove shared `library/`, saved workflow presets, other projects, other projects' references or any user-configured external asset folders.
- Reject deletion if **that project** has an active generation/workflow/refinement or another operation could write into its files. Prevent a race that recreates a supposedly deleted project. Surface a compact actionable error; never silently cancel another project’s work.
- Restrict filesystem operations to the verified gen3d-managed project UUID directory beneath the configured `GEN3D_DATA_DIR` (default `~/.gen3d`). Validate project identity/path; reject unknown IDs, symlink/path traversal and unsafe/unexpected targets. Do not allow arbitrary filesystem paths or whole-store deletion. Handle filesystem failures truthfully instead of reporting success while data remains.
- Keep destructive project deletion a **deliberate Web UI human action**; no automatic deletion during workflow cleanup, no MCP implicit approval or permission bypass. An HTTP endpoint such as `DELETE /api/projects/:id` may implement this, with the same actor checks as other human-only actions.
- Follow the visual-first UX direction from #28: icon/menu + short action + short confirmation, useful focus behavior, keyboard accessibility and no intrusive success explanation. Keep Light/Dark consistent.
- Project ID deletion does not delete the underlying imported or folder-backed assets; these are shared assets, not project-owned data. No backward-compatibility migration is needed.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] In both the Home project grid and/or project sidebar, the intended project has a clearly discoverable, keyboard-accessible Delete action (not confused with deletion of a model version or a workflow node).
- [ ] The single confirmation names the selected project and explicitly conveys permanent loss of **that project's** data; Cancel/Escape/closing it has no side effect; confirming sends only the selected project ID.
- [ ] Deleting an idle project actually removes its managed on-disk directory, its stored runs/checkpoints/images/GLBs/reviews and its listing; restart verifies the project stays gone and is not recreated.
- [ ] Delete one of multiple projects and verify every other project and the shared local asset library, external source paths and saved workflow presets remain unchanged. Deletion never removes assets that another project references.
- [ ] Active/in-progress target-project work blocks deletion, with a comprehensible error. Test the race between deletion and writes/restarts, and verify unknown IDs/path traversal/symlinks are rejected.
- [ ] After deletion, the Web UI clears a deleted current selection, updates the project list and displays a usable no-project empty state when applicable; other browser tabs can refresh correctly.
- [ ] The endpoint is limited to explicit permitted human Web UI actions, with no automatic or MCP-driven destructive bypass.
- [ ] Both display themes, narrow and desktop layouts, keyboard focus and dialog semantics work without extra instruction text. Browser checks cover deleting, cancelling and empty state.
- [ ] Run `npm test`, `npm run check` and relevant `npm run test:browser` tests; report results and any unperformed checks honestly. Update only the relevant brief README/usage guidance; avoid unrelated refactoring.

## Post-merge verification

None.

## Optional validation

- Brief hands-on check on a local instance with multiple disposable sample projects to verify that the project menu and one confirmation are immediately understandable.

## Context

- #3 — gen3d project vision
- #26 — current Home / Model studio / Workflow editor and checkpoint project model
- #28 — visual-first UX, fewer options/labels and unnecessary approvals
- Current implementation: `web/app.js` project grid/sidebar, `web/index.html` layouts, `src/server.js` project routes, `src/store.js` project directory and in-memory map.
- The default store is `~/.gen3d/` (or `GEN3D_DATA_DIR`), whose `library/` and `workflow-presets.json` are **shared** and must remain intact.

Implement the smallest correct project deletion flow. Do not substitute a documented manual `rm -r` procedure or hide/delete only the UI entry.
